headline: Spain's Late Blow Ends Portugal's Stubborn Rearguard
story: Spain suffocated Portugal in Dallas. Possession 51 per cent to 42, high-press sequences 9.0 to 4.1, forced turnovers 55 to 43—the numbers tell of relentless territorial dominance. Yet Spain wasted a big chance in the eighth minute. Portugal, passive and compact, managed only 2 shots on target from 10 attempts, but held firm until the 91st minute, when Spain finally converted and delivered the knockout blow.

Ball recovery time was Spain's lethal advantage: 13.8 seconds versus Portugal's 19.1 generated constant attacking flow. The xG gap—1.72 to 0.91—should have produced a wider margin. João Neves and Bruno Fernandes, Portugal's creative fulcrum, were systematically suffocated by Spain's press. A late Portuguese chance in the 90th minute (xG 0.16) was too desperate, too late. Spain's conversion in the 91st minute ended a match of Spanish dominance interrupted by frustration.

keyMoment.text: Spain's goal ended the siege—not a great chance (xG 0.55) but the only one that mattered.

home.verdict: Possession passivity and chance starvation made survival impossible.
points: Only 42% possession gave Spain perpetual attacking pressure; reactive football breeds defeat.

away.verdict: Unstoppable pressing and superior transitions won despite late finishing.
